First release of **Nest** — a local desktop workspace for persistent Codex and Claude Code agents that run on **your own ChatGPT and Claude subscriptions**, through the official tools already installed on your computer.

Nest never reads, copies or stores provider credentials, never scrapes chat websites and never calls undocumented endpoints. Inference goes to the provider you pick; agents, conversations, memory and activity stay in local SQLite.

## Downloads

| Platform | File |
| --- | --- |
| Windows 10/11 (x64) | `Nest.Setup.0.1.0.exe` — NSIS installer, per-user, desktop + Start Menu shortcuts |
| Linux (x64) | `Nest-0.1.0.AppImage` — portable, `chmod +x` and run |
| Debian / Ubuntu (x64) | `nest_0.1.0_amd64.deb` — `sudo apt install ./nest_0.1.0_amd64.deb` |

## Requirements

- Node.js 22.12+
- At least one provider signed in with a subscription:
  - **Codex** — `npm install -g @openai/codex`, then `codex login` (Sign in with ChatGPT)
  - **Claude Code** — `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`, then `claude auth login --claudeai`

Nest finds both on `PATH`, in their default install folders, or behind npm `.cmd` shims, and you can set explicit paths in Settings. It refuses to send messages while a provider is signed out, rate limited, or signed in with API-billed credentials unless you opt in; `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `*_BASE_URL` and similar variables are always stripped from provider processes so a stray key can't switch you to API billing.

## What's in it

- **Agents** with instructions, default provider and model, workspace folder, groups and permission defaults. Six templates: Chief of Staff, Researcher, Writer, Engineer, Outreach, Daily Briefer.
- **Native sessions per provider** — Codex threads resume with `thread/resume`, Claude sessions with `--session-id`/`--resume`. Switching provider hands the destination a bounded summary of only what it hasn't seen, instead of pretending sessions are shared.
- **Conservative permissions** by default: Claude Code `default` (ask), Codex `workspace-write` with `on-request` approvals. Bypass and full-access modes aren't offered. Permission prompts arrive in-app over stdio, so a run never blocks on a terminal Nest can't see.
- **Memory** as plain-text notes, per agent or shared, sent only when they change, with every run recording which notes it used.
- **Agent tools** over a local MCP server: agents can read their own profile, `remember` notes, `list_agents`, `delegate` to another agent (3 levels deep), and propose new agents, schedules or instruction changes behind an approval card.
- **Connectors** — agents use the MCP servers and apps you've already connected in each provider (Gmail, Calendar, Slack, …). Allow all, none, or only some, per agent and per provider. No connector credentials are stored.
- **Browser** — Claude Code agents can drive your real Chrome via Claude in Chrome, with an approval card per action. *(Windows only; Codex agents can't control a browser under `codex app-server`.)*
- **Routines** — run an agent daily, on weekdays, weekly, or every N minutes while Nest is open; runs missed while closed happen at next launch.
- **Handoffs** to another agent in a linked conversation, with results posted back to the source and the Inbox.
- **Voice dictation** — Whisper runs locally on your machine (transformers.js + ONNX Runtime); audio is never uploaded.
- **Cancel and restart safety** — cancelling interrupts the provider and then force-stops the process tree; anything still running when Nest closes is marked interrupted at next launch and pending approvals expire.
- Light/dark/system themes, text size, conversation width, and Markdown rendered without raw HTML.

## Notes

- Linux support is new in this release: the force-stop path now escalates a process-group `SIGTERM` to `SIGKILL`, so cancelling a wedged agent behaves as it does on Windows. The Chrome integration and provider auto-discovery in Windows install folders remain Windows-only.
- Installers are unsigned. Windows SmartScreen and Linux desktops may warn on first run.
- Nest is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by OpenAI or Anthropic. Codex, ChatGPT, Claude and Claude Code are their trademarks.
